Per-person modeling and the learning layer

epic.title: Epic 4: Everywhere via MCP and the CLI. One blazing-fast Rust binary
epic.body:
Living Brain is not only a Slack bot. Outside Slack, every surface reaches the same brain through two doors: **MCP** (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Claude Desktop and any other MCP client) and the **`livingbrain` CLI**. Both are one Rust binary: a single static executable, instant startup, a local cache so search answers before the network does.

**Stack.** A Rust Cargo workspace consumed as a Cratefield venture (`cratefield-core`, `cratefield-runtime-cloudflare`, modules from the harness repo by git until the 0.5 release round, [Cratefield/harness#464](https://github.com/Cratefield/harness/issues/464)), deployed as one Cloudflare Worker with D1, R2, KV and a venture-owned Durable Object, the same shape as `Owlpost-to/backend`. Modules only see ports (`Database`, `TextModel`, `Mailer`, `Realtime`, `Defer`, `Blob`, `KeyValue`, `Signer`, `Payments`); adapters are the only vendor-aware code. Email goes through **Owlpost** (Resend-compatible API, inbound agent inboxes).

**Rule.** MCP and the CLI are clients of the same API and the same `scopes_for` permission model. They never hold their own memory or their own agent loop; the local cache only ever holds pages the signed-in user may see.

**Children**
{{cli}} {{local_cache}} {{local_mcp}} {{claude_code}} {{agent_plugins}} {{perf}} {{pwa}} {{view3d}}

children.title: `livingbrain` CLI: one static Rust binary
children.body:
Part of {{epic}}. No dependencies inside the epic.

- Commands: `login` (device flow), `ask`, `search`, `note`, `page`, `export`, `mcp`.
- Static binary per target (macOS arm64/x64, Linux musl x64/arm64, Windows) via cargo-dist; Homebrew tap, `curl | sh`, npm shim.
- Pipes well: `git log -5 | livingbrain note --project api`; `--json` on every command for scripts and agents.
- Tokens in the OS keychain, never a dotfile.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] `livingbrain ask` returns a cited answer.
- [ ] Every command supports `--json`.
- [ ] No token is ever written to disk in plain text.

children.title: Local cache: instant search, offline reads
children.body:
Part of {{epic}}. Depends on {{cli}}.

- Sync the pages the user may see into a local SQLite (FTS5) cache, incrementally via a change feed; encrypted at rest with a key from the OS keychain.
- `search` and `page` answer from the cache first, then refresh; `ask` uses the cache as context and the server for the model.
- Logging out or losing access purges the cache.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] Search on a warm cache answers without a network call.
- [ ] Revoked access purges local pages on next sync (test).

children.title: MCP from the same binary: stdio and streamable HTTP
children.body:
Part of {{epic}}. Depends on {{cli}}, {{local_cache}}.

- `livingbrain mcp` serves the brain over stdio (and `--http` for clients that want streamable HTTP), backed by the local cache and the API. Same tools as the remote MCP server (Epic 3): `brain_search`, `brain_page`, `brain_context_for`, `brain_note`.
- Works in any MCP client: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Claude Desktop.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] The MCP Inspector lists and calls every tool.
- [ ] Tool results never include pages outside the user's scopes.

children.title: Claude Code: first-class plugin (MCP + skills + slash commands + hooks)
children.body:
Part of {{epic}}. Depends on {{local_mcp}}.

One install gives Claude Code the whole brain:
- The `livingbrain mcp` server, preconfigured.
- **Skills**: `brain-context` (pull conventions, owners and past decisions before coding), `brain-note` (record a decision with its reason).
- **Slash commands**: `/brain ask`, `/brain note`, `/brain colony` (start a Colonizer colony).
- **Hooks (opt-in)**: at session start, inject the brain's brief for this repo; at session end, send a redacted summary back (feeds the learning layer and the prompt library).
- Packaged as a Claude Code plugin in the Agent Plugins layout (`plugin.json`, `mcp.json`, `skills/`).

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] `/brain ask` returns a cited answer.
- [ ] The session-end hook redacts a planted fake key before upload (test).
- [ ] Hooks are off until the user opts in.

children.title: Same package for Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Claude Desktop
children.body:
Part of {{epic}}. Depends on {{claude_code}}.

- Reuse the plugin's MCP config and skills; `livingbrain mcp install <agent>` writes the right config (Codex `config.toml`, Cursor `mcp.json`, OpenCode, Claude Desktop).
- One docs page per agent with a one-line install.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] Each listed client can call `brain_search` after `livingbrain mcp install`.

children.title: Speed budget and benchmarks in CI
children.body:
Part of {{epic}}. Depends on {{cli}}, {{local_cache}}, {{local_mcp}}.

- Budgets: CLI cold start, warm-cache `search`, MCP `brain_search` round trip, binary size. Set them from the first measurements, then hold them.
- A benchmark job in CI (criterion + hyperfine) that fails on regression; publish the numbers in the README only once measured.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] CI fails when a budget regresses.
- [ ] No speed claim appears on the site before it is measured.

children.title: Easy to use: the web app as an installable, offline-first PWA
children.body:
Part of {{epic}}. Depends on {{local_cache}}.

Filed directly as #40; see the issue for the full body. Manifest + service worker, offline reads of permitted pages, one-tap sign-in, one search-or-ask box, share target, web push.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] Installs on iOS, Android and desktop.
- [ ] Logging out clears every cache.

children.title: `livingbrain view`: the 3D brain, locally, from the CLI
children.body:
Part of {{epic}}. Depends on {{cli}}, {{local_cache}}.

Filed directly as #41; see the issue for the full body. Loopback-only local server with a one-time token, same renderer as the site, offline from the cache.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] Binds to 127.0.0.1 only and rejects requests without the token.
